newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: DEL MONTE LAUNCHES MAJOR RESTRUCTURING.
newsitem.headline: DEL MONTE LAUNCHES MAJOR RESTRUCTURING.

text.p: South African food group Del Monte Royal Foods said on Wednesday it is to launch a restructuring of its operations which will cost 360 million rand.
The firm also said that due to the trading performance of its business it had elected to write down the value of its trademarks and brands by 1.2 billion rand.
Del Monte said it expected to reap the full benefits of the restructuring by the third year of its implementation. The benefits are estimated a 100 million rand per year.

The group said in a statement accompanying first half results that of the 360 million rand cost of the programme, 20 million rand related to Del Monte Europe and another 30 million to the group's 50 percent share in Nabisco SA, which is part of the U.S. biscuits giant RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp .
The 228 million rand cash part would be financed substantially from the proposed sale of non-core Italian assets.
Del Monte said that the disruption arising from the restructuring programme in Europe made it very difficult to forecast the performance of the European operations for the rest of the year.
However, the Phillipines operation and Nabisco SA were expected to show an improvement in the second half of the year.

"The directors believe they have identified steps to be taken to put the business on a sound footing, which should enable the group to show steadily improving results in future years," the group said.
Del Monte reported a slide in half year headline earnings to 11.7 cents a share from 17.8 cents before. It did not declare it dividend.
The group last month issued a profit warning.

Vivian Imerman, Del Monte's head, said that the operations restructuring would embrace a wide range of activities including a rationalisation of the customer base, a cutback in sales activities, the consolidation of certain factories, changes in distribution network, the rationalisation of certain product lines and office reorganisations.
Critical mass would also be built through strategic alliances, Imerman said.
The restructuring, announced at the time of the 1996 results release, followed a strategic review which identified that the group's problems were both external and internal, he said.

"The external factors include export subsidy removals both from South Africa and Kenya of 60-70 million rand per annum, continued and increasing trade concentration in Europe and volatility in currencies and raw material prices," Imerman said.

The internal factors included the collapse of the Italian unit's profitability due to poor managerial and strategic decisions. Marketing activity had also not been sufficiently focused on core brands, he said.
The review process had identified unexploited potential in existing lines of business, Imerman said.

The group said that Del Monte Europe was the main contributor to the slide in half year earnings. This was mainly due to the disruptions arising from the restructuring programme, unspecified difficulties in Italy, certain adverse currency movements and reduced volumes.
